Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jamal Chen (Redwood Runtime Eng), Marcus Gray (Peregrine ML Platform), Priya Nair (Peregrine ML Eng), Olivier DuPont (Peregrine Infra), Sara Khan (Peregrine Security)
summary: Engineering deep dive to reconcile cost vs latency for hybrid MoE routing across Llama/Mistral/Qwen model variants, investigate ROPE scaling and token-affinity effects on routing stability, discuss KV cache warm strategies in a VPC/on-prem context, and plan a short lab to validate tradeoffs. Customer provided high-level SLOs and sample traffic characteristics; Redwood to provide microbenchmarks and assist with trace-driven simulations.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): okay hi everyone thanks for carving the time, this is Samir from Redwood, we wanted to go deep on the hybrid MoE routing and the ROPE scaling stuff — try to keep to engineering details and leave pricing to the end.
[00:14] Marcus (Peregrine): hey thanks, yeah we had a couple of outages when the routing spiked, and the token affinity seems to drift after long contexts.
[00:26] Elena (Redwood SE): uh-huh, thanks Marcus, and Priya mentioned there are mixed models in the stack — Llama 70b, Mistral large-1, and a Qwen variant?
[00:36] Priya (Peregrine): yes correct, Llama for in-context reasoning, Mistral on user-facing completions, Qwen for retrieval-augmented responses. We're using an MoE layer for routing certain instruction signals to smaller experts to save cost.
[00:50] Jamal (Redwood): quick clarifying q, are you running routing on-host (customer infra) or on Redwood Dedicated nodes?
[00:56] Olivier (Peregrine): currently on our VPC, we frontload to dedicated infra but want to push more to on-prem in EU region next quarter.
[01:05] Samir: got it. ok first slide — ROPE / positional decay and why it matters for routing. when you lengthen contexts, the positional encodings drift and token affinity becomes less stable so tokens that previously routed to the same expert start going elsewhere — this increases cold KV lookups and routing churn which spikes latency.
[01:29] Priya: can you say 'ROPE drift' again — sometimes our SREs call it rowp decay, same thing?
[01:34] Elena: it's the same notion, people say ROPE or 'rowp' in speech transcripts a lot — it's rotary positional embeddings. the main variables are base frequency and scaling schedule. if you compress the rope scaling you reduce drift but you may lose relative position sensitivity for long-range tasks.
[01:55] Marcus: and that was our main issue — for long threads (~4k tokens) the routing changed mid-session and we'd see a 2-3x increase in per-token latency.
[02:08] Jamal: yeah that sounds like KV cache misses. if the routing flips the KV context is on different hosts or different shard and you get cache miss + network fetch. in VPC that hits internal cross-az bandwidth and adds 40-120ms in our trials.
[02:24] Olivier: our infra shows spikes to 220ms tail during those events.
[02:29] Samir: okay so three levers: 1) ROPE scaling tweaks, 2) routing smoothing / token-affinity stabilization, 3) KV prewarm and shard co-location. we'll go through them.
[02:43] [03:00] Elena: on ROPE tuning, one approach is to bias the base frequency (alpha) so the embeddings decay slower — that keeps affinity more stable at long context sizes. downside: it compresses high-frequency positional cues. for generative tasks you might reduce long-range hallucinations but you can harm some math reasoning signals; it's workload-dependent.
[03:28] Priya: we ran a quick ab on alpha = 240 vs 512 and saw minor perplexity changes but routing instability improved. however, Qwen's expert selector seems more sensitive.
[03:41] Samir: that's useful — model sensitivity differs. Redwood Optimize can recommend alpha per model/workload but you should validate. we'll share our per-model profiles.
[03:51] Marcus: on routing smoothing — what are the practical techniques?
[03:55] Jamal: exponential smoothing on logits, i.e., maintain an EMA of recent router logits per token prefix and interpolate between current logits and EMA before argmax / sampling. it stabilizes routing but can slightly increase load on hot experts since smoothing favors previous choices.
[04:12] Olivier: does that mean we risk overloading a single expert and getting queuing?
[04:15] Jamal: yes that's the tradeoff; we add a cap and backlog-aware rerouting: if an expert's queue depth exceeds threshold, we degrade smoothing and allow reroute. Redwood runtime supports that policy.
[04:29] [04:40] Elena: also look at token affinity hashing — prefix-hash + local affinity table keeps short-term affinity sticky without requiring cross-host state. cheaper but less robust for long-range drift.
[04:58] Priya: and for KV cache prewarm, what are the options? we've got hot prefixes for chat sessions and some background LLM-based functions.
[05:07] Samir: simplest is on-demand prewarm: when a session enters a 'hot' state (identified by prefix fingerprint) you asynchronously fetch KV shards to the node that will likely serve, then warm local cache. more complex: predictive prewarm using recent traces. Redwood can ingest a 1k-request trace and compute a prewarm schedule.
[05:27] Marcus: yeah we have traces but they're messy — Priya can extract.
[05:32] Priya: will do. quick question on shard co-location — is it possible to pin experts and KV shards to the same affinity group?
[05:39] Jamal: we support affinity groups. if you pin experts + KV shards to the same host pool you reduce cross-host fetches. downside: reduces placement flexibility and can affect utilization during skew.
[05:51] [06:00] Sara (Security): a security question — prewarming means more data movement inside our VPC. does Redwood provide audit logs and KMS integration for those flows?
[06:09] Samir: yes, logs are auditable; prewarm fetches are recorded in the audit stream. we integrate with customer KMS for any secrets. for on-prem there are options to keep trace material local and only share metadata with Redwood control plane.
[06:25] Sara: okay thanks.
[06:29] Marcus: jumping back to cost tradeoffs — how do we compute expected per-token cost with hybrid routing?
[06:36] Elena: you model expected expert fanout and multiply by expert execution cost plus KV fetch probability * network egress cost. we have a simple estimator spreadsheet we'll share; but the unknown is routing entropy — high entropy increases average experts per token.
[06:52] Priya: is there a way to cap fanout deterministically? like top-1 routing?
[06:58] Jamal: top-1 routing is the cheapest but brittle. Top-k with pruning is common: restrict k dynamically based on load. Redwood supports dynamic k with fallback to denser models when cost budget is exceeded.
[07:14] Marcus: err we've seen poorer quality with top-1 on certain prompt types. the user experience degraded.
[07:19] Samir: that's expected. you can also hybridize: top-1 in steady-state, and ramp to top-2/3 when prompt uncertainty crosses a threshold. thresholding can be based on softmax gap or calibrated confidence.
[07:33] [07:40] Elena: quantization — we need to call out effect on routing. 8-bit quantization of experts' weights can change logits distribution and the router may pick different experts. we've observed small but actionable shifts. recommended practice: keep the router at higher precision (e.g., float16) and quantize experts first, validate routing stability.
[08:00] Priya: that was our suspicion — we quantized everything to int8 to save cost and routing became noisy.
[08:06] Jamal: yes, router sensitivity matters. alternative is per-layer mixed precision: router in fp16, expert weights int8. Redwood runtime supports mixed precision execution to preserve router fidelity.
[08:19] Olivier: any guidance for models shared across Llama and Mistral? their tokenization differences change prefix alignment and can affect hash-based affinity, right?
[08:29] Elena: correct. when combining models with different tokenizers, normalize prefixes to a canonical token boundary or run routing on semantic features downstream of tokenization, e.g., n-gram embedding fingerprint. it's more compute but improves cross-model routing stability.
[08:44] Marcus: ok that seems heavy. is there a middle ground?
[08:48] Samir: short-term: normalize whitespace and run a lightweight byte-level hash to reduce variance; long-term: semantic routing if you have the cycles.
[08:59] [09:10] Priya: network egress — in our VPC we saw cross-az charges escalate when KV misses occurred frequently. what's Redwood's recommendation?
[09:18] Jamal: two options: co-locate hot shards to the same AZ, or use predictive prewarm to avoid cross-AZ fetch. We also support a local fallback where a small resident expert replica handles requests during fetch, returning slightly degraded but bounded results.
[09:35] Olivier: that local fallback is interesting — what's the quality delta typically?
[09:39] Elena: depends — usually 2-5% relative metric drop on our evals for the degraded local expert but latency improves dramatically. it's workload-dependent.
[09:48] Marcus: could we configure an SLA-triggered fallback? like when tail latency > 200ms switch to local-only mode?
[09:56] Jamal: yes we can hook that into our runtime policies.
[09:59] [10:10] Samir: moving to concrete lab plan — Redwood will run a three-scenario microbenchmark: baseline (no smoothing, default ROPE), ROPE-adjusted (alpha tuned), and smoothing + prewarm. we'll run across Llama70, Mistral-large, Qwen-45 styles with our customer's trace.
[10:27] Priya: what metrics will you collect?
[10:29] Samir: per-token latency P50/P90/P99, expert fanout distribution, KV miss rate, cross-az bytes, and quality delta (BLEU/perp/our supplied eval prompts).
[10:40] Marcus: cool. also include a scenario with int8 experts and fp16 router.
[10:45] Jamal: yes we'll add the mixed-precision scenario.
[10:48] [11:00] Elena: note on instrumentation: ensure you capture router logits and softmax gap over time; that'll help tune smoothing window and threshold.
[11:09] Priya: ok we'll redact PII and send trace.
[11:13] Samir: perfect. security note: use the pre-signed upload link we sent and it will be stored in your VPC bucket that Redwood can access only via TLS with customer KMS key.
[11:25] Sara: that addresses the audit piece. one more ask — can we get SOC2 documentation before pilot?
[11:31] Samir: yes we'll attach SOC2 and ISO certs in the follow-up email.
[11:35] Marcus: great.
[11:38] [11:50] Priya: curious question — we sometimes see routing noise after model updates. how to prevent rollouts from causing affinity flips?
[11:46] Jamal: rollout strategy: canary with routing compatibility checks. before switching traffic, compute expected router-output overlap between versions on a sample of traces; if overlap drops below threshold, fail the rollout or run soft-routing where both experts are warmed and results are ensembled for a short window.
[12:04] Samir: Redwood Console can run that compatibility check automatically as part of the rollout pipeline.
[12:09] Marcus: excellent.
[12:12] [12:25] Elena: small gotcha — ROPE scaling interacts with position-sensitive features like timestamps or tokens inserted by retrieval augmentation; be careful when you tune ROPE in a retrieval-heavy workload.
[12:35] Priya: ok noted.
[12:38] Jamal: another operational tip: maintain a small sticky KV replica (mini-shard) per node that holds the last N prefixes for that session cluster — it's cheap and mitigates brief routing flips.
[12:51] Olivier: what's N typically?
[12:53] Jamal: 50-200 prefixes depending on memory budget. we saw big wins with 100 in most chat workloads.
[12:59] [13:10] Samir: wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners. we'll share the bench spreadsheet, Peregrine will upload trace, and we'll run the three-scenario lab and present results next week.
[13:24] Marcus: thanks all, that was really productive.
[13:29] Sara: appreciated.
[13:32] Samir: okay we'll follow up with SOC2 and microbench link. thanks everyone.
[13:39] [End of recording]
questions: How to stabilize routing for long contexts?
What are the tradeoffs of ROPE alpha adjustments?
Can we reduce KV cross-AZ egress with prewarm and affinity?
